overlay.note: Every session reads slot A and the window's capital vector table back after START GAME and compares them with the restore run and the reader's table image. The forced session zeroes both at the reader's entry, as a boss overlay would, and must reach gameplay with the shipped bytes back. Frames are EMULATOR.

boot_smoke.blank_window_rule: every frame from power-on, and from the frame after RESET, until the splash display after start: at most 64 visible pixels (one 8x8 cell, the OS cursor) outside the frame's two most frequent colours

heaviest_frame_cost_breakdown.synchronization_note: Measurement begins after wait_frame; gameplay DLI service is included in vbi_and_synchronization.

historical_runtime_headroom_gate.note: The feature gate is additional; this historical checkpoint remains explicit.

instrumentation.start_semantics: first instruction after wait_frame returns, before the released OPTION poll
instrumentation.end_semantics: first instruction of the next wait_frame call
instrumentation.nmi_note: The release deliberately enables both gameplay DLIs and leaves OS VBI NMI disabled; Atari800_nframes supplies the host/VBI boundary identifier.

replay.input: production frontend/options handlers followed by deterministic held-FIRE neutral/sweep/evasive/hunt joystick policies

boss_edge_guard.clause: parked at HPOS 48, firing, MEDIUM: at least one Interceptor escort and one hit on the player in the first 4000 frames of the fight

boss_row_switches.clause: every band frame (phase 0 and phase 1 ran: drawn to the band's end) shows exactly its region's row switches, each on its row's first line, its colour stores done by cycle 14

director_heaviest_frame.clause: the heaviest frame with a Director request, event or world-row tick fits the gates: fence margin >= 500, DMA-on <= 32,568

boss_entry_debris.clause: no debris live on the boss entry frame (ENTITY_ACTIVE_MASK bit 0 clear on the entry row), over every boss entry of the run

boss_entry_hud.clause: the HUD row (40 cells) when the install first reaches the main loop equals the row as the boss entry began, over every boss entry of the run

slot_f_writes.clause: slot F ($5200-$53FF) is written only by the start-up writers (those that wrote it before the first copy_hud_charset - a RESET runs them again), the charset copy, the sector reader's region block read at a boss entry, and the field's code into its own state bytes, in every replay and boot-smoke session

window_tail_writes.clause: the window's unclaimed tail (the window's end to $BBFF) is written only by the start-up writers, the sector reader's read of the lance run into the lance's RAM at a boss entry, and the lance's own code into its own RAM, in every replay (decision BD 6)

hud_row_writers.note: every writer of $4000-$4027 in every phase (frontend, summary and reader screens share the row's RAM)

light_archetypes.clause: L1 a live Interceptor Light; L2 two or more Lights live at once; L3 no Heavy live in a swarm sector; L4 at most one live Light in an elite sector; L5 a variant (a) formation flies with its Interceptor - each over a non-empty subject, boss rows apart

maximum_projectile_pool.scope: combined active PlayerFighter and Interceptor fighter-projectile slots in legal Atari800 replays
maximum_projectile_pool.evidence_note: The physical 10-slot PairShot allocation was reached by a legal replay; 10/10 is observed rather than inferred or artificially seeded.

broadside_projectiles.classification: observed through the production scheduler during the natural first capital-section pass on EASY, MEDIUM, and HARD; no phase, world row, muzzle, projectile, object, or intensity state was seeded

limitations: This is exact emulated ANTIC master-clock timing for Atari800 7.1.2, not an electrical measurement from a physical 65XE.
The bounded deterministic replay is reproducible coverage, not a proof over every possible joystick history.
Atari800 host-frame boundaries occur at the PAL frame wrap; the gameplay scheduler synchronises at VCOUNT $70, so missed_frames is derived from the exact next start host-frame ID.
The release enables DLI NMI ($80), not OS VBI NMI ($40); enabling OS VBI would change the accepted production runtime.
